sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell in Fort Lauderdale, FL?
sections.html:
The quickest route is a direct cash sale, where the buyer accepts the home in its present condition and closes once title is clear. In Fort Lauderdale the details to settle first are who owns the property, what is owed against it and whether anyone lives in it.

Fort Lauderdale is the largest of Broward County's 31 municipalities, according to the city, and one of the ten largest cities in Florida. Every property has its own loose ends: a mortgage payoff, a tenant's lease or an estate that has not yet been opened. This page sets out the local facts and state rules that bear on each one.

sections.h2: How pricey is housing in Fort Lauderdale?
sections.html:
Fort Lauderdale's QuickFacts page estimates a July 2025 population of 188,677, a gain of 3.3 percent over the April 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it counts 80,999 households and shows an owner-occupied median value of $486,700, and 54.1 percent of units lived in by the people who own them.

Costs are high. Median monthly owner costs are $2,679 for owners paying a mortgage and $1,122 for those who are not, while the gross rent median is $1,854 and household income has a median of $83,130 in 2024 dollars.

  • Renters live in a large share of homes.
  • The city has 34.59 square miles of land area and a 2020 density near 5,284 people per square mile.
  • Residents 65 and over are 19.6 percent of the population.

With values near $486,700, the deed stamps and exemption rules below deserve a close look.

sections.h2: Where does Fort Lauderdale's name come from?
sections.html:
The city takes its name from a Second Seminole War fort built on the New River in 1838, when Major William Lauderdale led Tennessee Volunteers south along the east coast. Three forts carried his name: one at the fork of the New River, one at Tarpon Bend and the largest on the beach at the site of Bahia Mar. None survive. Fort Lauderdale became a city on March 27, 1911, spanning roughly 36 square miles.

It counts about 165 miles of inland waterways, which earned the nickname Venice of America, and more than 3,000 hours of sun a year. Its economy now spans marine trades, manufacturing, finance, insurance, real estate, aerospace and film production.

sections.h2: Who lives in Fort Lauderdale and how does that shape buyers?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a varied population: 27.0 percent foreign-born, and 30.1 percent of residents over age 5 use a different language at home. 40.8 percent of adults 25 and up hold a four-year degree or higher, and 84.4 percent kept their address from the year before.

The mean commute is 26.1 minutes, and 91.8 percent of households have broadband. Working households with long local ties and many older residents shape the buyer pool.

The city points to the Riverwalk arts and science district, Las Olas Boulevard and a downtown that includes Broward College and Florida Atlantic University. Homes near them can suit buyers who want a short commute.

sections.h2: How does Broward County handle homestead after a Fort Lauderdale sale?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser says all legal Florida residents may qualify for homestead on a home they make their permanent residence as of January 1. Its page reports that the basic exemption saved a Broward homeowner between $673 and $1,020 in 2026, depending on the city's millage rate, for homes valued at $75,000 or higher.

Deadlines are strict. The office states that the timely filing period for 2027 runs from March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027, and that the last day to late file any 2027 exemption is September 20, 2027. It adds that state law bars late filing after that date regardless of good cause. For 2026, the timely deadline was March 2, and the late-filing deadline of September 18, 2026 has passed.

A sale ends the seller's exemption, and the Save Our Homes assessment resets to just value on the January 1 after a change of ownership, per the Department of Revenue. Any buyer should file their own application.

sections.h2: What should a Fort Lauderdale seller do about the March and September homestead dates?
sections.html:
Timing decides whether a buyer gets the exemption in the first year. The Broward appraiser stresses that state law bars late filing for any exemption after the September deadline, whatever the reason for missing it.

  • For 2026, the timely deadline was March 2 and the late-filing deadline of September 18, 2026 has passed.
  • For 2027, the timely deadline is March 1, 2027 and the last late-filing day is September 20, 2027.
  • For 2028, the timely window runs March 2, 2027 through March 1, 2028, with a late-filing limit of September 18, 2028.

Pass these dates to your buyer at closing so the application is filed on time.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs on a Fort Lauderdale sale?
sections.html:
Broward uses the standard deed rate of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, because only Miami-Dade differs. Every party to the deed is liable, and the Broward clerk takes payment at recording. Per-page recording fees come from section 28.24.

Fort Lauderdale seller checklist with the office that handles each item

Ask your title company for a closing statement that shows each charge before signing.

sections.h2: What if my Fort Lauderdale house has a tenant?
sections.html:
A tenant does not block a sale, but the notice rules for ending a tenancy still apply. Florida's chapter 83 sets short written notices for unpaid rent and for lease violations, and longer notices that depend on how often rent is paid, including a monthly-tenancy rule.

Ask whether the buyer will keep the tenant under the current lease, which avoids notice and court steps. If you need the tenant to leave, speak with a Florida landlord-tenant attorney before serving any notice.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Fort Lauderdale house?
sections.html:
Most buyers want proof that someone has authority to sign for the estate. A smaller estate may qualify for summary administration, which is a streamlined court process, and creditors have a set period to file claims.

Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004, and a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxed for stamps. Ask the Broward County Clerk of Courts or a probate attorney which procedure fits your situation.

sections.h2: What paperwork do Broward sellers and new owners need for homestead?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser asks applicants to bring proof of ownership, usually the recorded deed in the applicant's name, and notes that deeds already recorded in Broward's Official Records need not be copied. Where co-owners hold as tenants in common, every owner who lives there must file to claim full coverage.

For married couples and joint tenants with right of survivorship, any one owner may qualify for full coverage, though the office says it is advisable for all eligible owner-occupants to file. If the house is held in a trust, the office has separate requirements, so contact it before the sale.

  • Bring identification and proof the home is your permanent residence as of January 1.
  • Apply online through the office's portal or in person.
  • Ask the office about a mobile exemption event if travel is hard.

faqs.q: What do home values look like in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: QuickFacts shows $486,700 for 2020 to 2024, and 54.1 percent of homes lived in by owners.

faqs.q: When is the Broward homestead deadline?
faqs.a: Each March 1. For 2027 the office lists a timely period through March 1, 2027 and a final late-filing date of September 20, 2027.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Broward?
faqs.a: No. Only Miami-Dade has a different rate. Broward charges the flat state rate, 70 cents for each $100 paid, and the clerk collects it at recording.

faqs.q: How long does a month-to-month Broward tenant have to leave?
faqs.a: Chapter 83 sets the minimum notice for each type of periodic tenancy, so check the statute or ask an attorney before serving notice.

faqs.q: Is a probate house sellable in Broward?
faqs.a: Usually after the personal representative has court authority, or the estate has finished a short process. A probate attorney can confirm which applies.
